question: For a basic rural roadside sign, combine Figure 2A-2 with Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 to state the normal minimum mounting height and lateral offset.
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a typical roadside sign in a rural area, the normal minimum mounting height is 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement (Section 2A.15). Figure 2A-2 (Panels A and B) shows the normal lateral offset as a minimum of 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder where the shoulder is wider than 6 feet; Section 2A.16 addresses lateral offsets, including the 6-foot minimum for overhead sign supports and reduced offsets in constrained areas. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For comparison in developed areas: "In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height... of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For overhead supports (the offset provision quoted in the available evidence): "For overhead sign supports, the minimum lateral offset from the edge of the shoulder (or if no shoulder exists, from the edge of the pavement) to the near edge of overhead sign supports (cantilever or sign bridges) shall be 6 feet." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2, Panel A ("Roadside sign in rural area") shows a STOP sign with "12 ft MIN." lateral offset from the edge of the traveled way and "5 ft MIN." mounting height, while Panel B shows "6 ft MIN." offset from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet with the same "5 ft MIN." height. - [Image 2] The full page containing Figure 2A-2 confirms these dimensions and notes that Section 2A.16 allows reduced lateral offsets where offsets are limited. - [Image 3] Figure 2M-3 (recreational/cultural signs) repeats the same rural pattern: "12 ft MIN." from the edge of the traveled way (or "6 ft MIN." from a paved shoulder) with "5 ft MIN." height. - [Image 4] Figure 2A-3's note states: "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way," confirming the normal roadside offset values. - [Image 5] The page containing Sections 2A.15/2A.16 shows the mounting height standards and the beginning of the Lateral Offset section. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 2A.16 Standard §1 (p.59) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Page 92 - Page 566 - Page 100 - Page 93
gold_answer: The minimum mounting height is 5 feet. The normal minimum lateral offset is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet.
